name: Environmental impact of inhalers - Prescribing of inhalers (excluding salbutamol) with low Global Warming Potential (GWP)
description: Inhalers with low Global Warming Potential (GWP) prescribed as a proportion of all inhalers in BNF Chapter 3, excluding salbutamol
y_label: Percentage of non-salbutamol inhalers prescribed as higher GWP
why_it_matters: The updated BTS/NICE/SIGN guidance on asthma management recommends basing inhaler choice on:
• the preference of the person receiving the treatment
• the lowest environmental impact among suitable devices
• the presence of an integral dose counter.
The NHS has committed to reducing its carbon footprint by 80% by 2028 to 2032,
including a shift to lower carbon inhalers. Dry powder inhalers (DPIs) and other newer types of inhalers like soft
mist inhalers are less harmful to the environment than traditional metered dose inhalers (MDIs).
MDI devices using the newer propellant HFO-1234ze are considered low GWP under this measure, reflecting that the greenhouse gas emissions are considered to be
similar to a DPI on a per-dose basis.
produced a inhaler decision aid to facilitiate discussion about inhaler options.
